countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

Graduates move into manufacturing, automotive, energy, thermal and design roles, or continue to a master's specialisation such as thermal engineering or machine design.

universities.summary: Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence is a private, fully residential research university on a 286-acre campus near Greater Noida in the Delhi National Capital Region. Founded in 2011 and declared an Institution of Eminence Deemed to be University in 2022, it teaches four-year undergraduate degrees in engineering, natural sciences, social sciences, design and management.
universities.campusLifestyle: The 286-acre campus houses more than 2,500 students and over 250 faculty and staff across four Schools: Engineering, Natural Sciences, Humanities and Social Sciences, and Management and Entrepreneurship. On-campus services include a central library, cafes, grocery stores, an indoor sports complex, a student recreation centre, a post office, a salon and an in-house bank with ATMs. The academic year runs from August to May with a winter break in December, and students come from 28 Indian states.
universities.cityProfile: The campus sits on NH-91 in Dadri tehsil of Gautam Buddha Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh, inside the Delhi National Capital Region; NIRF records the university under Gautam Buddha Nagar. Because the university is fully residential, day-to-day life is centred on campus rather than on a city neighbourhood. University-chartered buses run on weekends, on a paid basis, between the campus and the Great India Place mall in Noida, and students who need hospital care beyond the campus health centre are referred to Kailash Hospital, Yatharth Hospital or Fortis Hospital in Greater Noida. The university describes its NCR location as giving students access to Delhi's cultural and recreational life, but international arrivals should plan onward transport from Delhi to the campus before travelling.
universities.practicalExposure: Undergraduate degrees at Shiv Nadar are four-year programmes with a research orientation: the sciences and social sciences carry the '(Research)' label in their titles, and the university describes itself as the first in India to offer a four-year multidisciplinary research degree. The Department of Computer Science and Engineering, one of the largest in the School of Engineering, lists research groups including algorithms and complexity and natural language processing. The International Office runs outbound mobility with partner universities, including semester exchanges, summer schools, full-year engagements and research internships, with pre-departure orientation for selected students. Students who want a US degree can take the BS Computer Science or BS Business 2+2 dual degree, studying two years in Delhi-NCR and two at Arizona State University, where the university estimates about USD 45,000 tuition and USD 15,000 living costs a year. A Career Development Centre prepares students for placements and graduate study, and on-campus jobs open after the first semester.
universities.hostelOverview: Shiv Nadar is fully residential. Gender-segregated hostels are spread over 18 buildings with twin and single rooms, AC and non-AC, some with attached bathrooms, allotted by course and availability. Each hostel has wardens, 24/7 security, power backup and internet, Wi-Fi in common areas, and air-conditioned 24x7 study rooms under CCTV with access control. For the 2026 intake, living charges are INR 2,43,500 a year for AC twin sharing or INR 2,28,500 for non-AC twin sharing, covering hostel, mess, laundry and 24x7 primary medical services. A higher room category, if allotted, is billed extra.
universities.dietarySupport: Mess charges are included in the annual living charge. Four meals are served daily (breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner), plus a midnight mess from 23:00 to 02:00. The mess is run by Sodexo under Food Safety and Standards Authority of India parameters, with menus set with student representatives. Students with food allergies can arrange special meals through the Department of Student Affairs with medical documents. Hostel pantries have microwaves and induction cooktops for light snacks; cooking in rooms is not allowed.
universities.safetyOverview: The Health and Wellness Centre has a general physician, nursing staff and ambulances available 24/7, with an Advanced Life Support ambulance for transfers to tertiary hospitals. All students are covered by group medical insurance with cashless hospitalisation up to INR 2.5 lakh. Campus security handles safety reports, and the university follows zero tolerance on ragging, with an annual anti-ragging affidavit required for enrolment.
universities.studentSupport: Every international student is assigned a Campus Buddy, a student volunteer who helps with settling in. Two clinical psychologists live on campus, and a YourDOST partnership gives 24x7 online counselling on helpline 1800 891 3499; primary medical and counselling services are free. Family Groups led by senior students and Peer Support Guides help first-year undergraduates adjust.

faq.question: Is Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence public or private?
faq.answer: It is private. It was established in 2011 as Shiv Nadar University under Uttar Pradesh Act No. 12 of 2011. On 3 August 2022 the Ministry of Education declared it an Institution of Eminence Deemed to be University, and the UGC removed it from its list of state private universities from that date. It is now known as Shiv Nadar (Institution of Eminence Deemed to be University).

faq.question: What language are the programmes taught in?
faq.answer: English. The university is listed by the University of Michigan's Rackham Graduate School among overseas institutions whose language of instruction is English exclusively. Most non-engineering programmes require English as a Class 12 subject, while English is not mandatory for IB and Cambridge applicants. The admissions pages do not list a separate IELTS or TOEFL requirement for international applicants.

faq.question: Can I apply straight after finishing school?
faq.answer: Yes. Entry is straight after Class 12 or an equivalent school-leaving qualification. You need an aggregate of at least 65 per cent across all subjects, including the subjects named for your programme, such as Physics and Mathematics for most B.Tech. degrees, and a pass in every subject. IB students need 28 of 45 points or 65 per cent, and Cambridge students need two A levels and 65 per cent Percentage Uniform Mark.

faq.question: How much does a year cost?
faq.answer: For the 2026 intake, first-year tuition is INR 6,00,000 for Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Design, Economics and Management; INR 4,25,000 for Mechanical, Civil and Chemical Engineering; and INR 4,00,000 for the natural sciences and International Relations. Living charges add INR 2,43,500 (AC twin) or INR 2,28,500 (non-AC twin). One-time charges are INR 2,500, INR 60,000 and a refundable INR 30,000 deposit. Charges can rise by up to 8 per cent a year.

faq.question: Do international students pay a different fee?
faq.answer: Shiv Nadar last published a separate foreign-national fee table for the 2024 cycle, and it was in Indian rupees. For 2026 only the common undergraduate fee table is published, so the rupee figures above are a planning estimate for international applicants. The binding figure is the one in your offer letter.

faq.question: How do I apply as an international student?
faq.answer: Apply online through the university's international application form at ugapplications.snu.edu.in. You can choose several admission routes in the same form. Foreign passport holders, including OCI and PIO card holders, apply in the foreign national or NRI category. Indian nationals who completed Class 12 outside India are also treated as international applicants.

faq.question: Which entrance test do I need?
faq.answer: International applicants usually use a valid SAT or ACT score or the university's own SNUSAT. SNUSAT is an online, home-proctored test of quantitative and logical reasoning, held in six cycles from January to July. B.Tech. and BS Computer Science applicants on the SNUSAT route also take the APT in Physics and Mathematics. JEE Main and CUET are accepted too, and design applicants add a portfolio review and interview.

faq.question: When is the intake and when should I apply?
faq.answer: There is one intake a year, in August, and the academic year runs from August to May. For 2026, the last application window ran from 1 to 15 June, with SNUSAT on 22 June, offers on 30 June and fee payment by 8 July. Earlier phases closed on 30 April and 31 May. Apply in the earliest phase you can, so there is time to get a student visa after your offer.

faq.question: Is the university recognised?
faq.answer: Yes. The UGC lists Shiv Nadar as an Institution of Eminence, notified on 3 August 2022, one of four private institutions on that list of twelve. NAAC lists it as accredited with grade A (CGPA 3.06, first cycle, declared 26 November 2019). In the NIRF India Rankings 2025 it placed 57th among universities and 85th overall. Recognition of the degree abroad depends on the credential-evaluation body in your destination country.

faq.question: What accommodation is available and what does it cost?
faq.answer: The campus is fully residential. Gender-segregated hostels across 18 buildings offer twin and single rooms, AC and non-AC, some with attached bathrooms, allotted by course and availability. For 2026, AC twin sharing costs INR 2,43,500 a year and non-AC twin sharing INR 2,28,500. Both include hostel, mess with four daily meals, laundry and 24x7 primary medical services.

faq.question: Are scholarships open to international students?
faq.answer: The 2026 list includes School Topper's, merit-based, JEE and UCEED, Vice-Chancellor's (up to INR 1 lakh a year for top SNUSAT performers), sports and need-based awards. The 2026 page does not say which of these apply to foreign nationals. The 2024 international page offered a 50 per cent School Topper's waiver and a 25 per cent merit waiver, for example for IB scores of 40 or more. Need-based aid relies on Indian financial documents.

faq.question: What is the dual degree with Arizona State University?
faq.answer: The BS Computer Science and BS Business (2+2) programmes run two years at Shiv Nadar's Delhi-NCR campus and two years at Arizona State University in the US. Tuition for the Indian years is INR 8,00,000 a year for the 2026 intake. For the ASU years, the university estimates about USD 45,000 in tuition and USD 15,000 in living costs a year, based on its 2028-29 projection.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
